fatal_errors: The proposed chemical dealloying method is not the reported spray-drying/thermal decomposition-reduction method.
The assumed sacrificial-element precursor alloy is incompatible with the actual homogeneous spray-dried salt precursor particles.
The response omits the essential H2 reduction at 300°C and the noble-metal-seeded, hydrogen-assisted reduction mechanism.
No evidence is cited to support dealloying as the method used in the target work.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses formation of porous HEA three-dimensional frameworks and proposes testable microscopy, surface-area, and catalytic measurements, but it reconstructs a fundamentally different synthesis route. The target uses spray drying of mixed salts followed by low-temperature H2 thermal decomposition-reduction, producing nanoarm-based frameworks through Pt-, Ir-, or Ru-seeded hydrogen-assisted reduction. It does not rely on selective dissolution of sacrificial elements. The predicted benefits of porosity and increased catalytic area are only broadly consistent, while the specific MOR comparison with Pt black, phase control, composition limits, and fcc-to-hcp transformation are absent. Because the alternative is generic and has no supporting evidence, it is unsupported rather than a well-supported plausible alternative.
